open-question.id: Recommendation run commit subject and body
open-question.question: The inline recommendation pass commits once per run with its reasoning in the commit body. What is the subject (for example Recommendation-annotation: <milestone_id>), and what shape does the body take: one line per question in the lifted option-and-rationale form, or free prose covering the whole set?
open-question.alternative: The pass commits once under `Recommendation-annotation: <milestone_id>` — today's marker with the whole-run descriptor every once-per-run committer here already carries — and its body is one `lift`-printed "`<option>` — `<rationale>`" line per question the run annotated, gathered after the embeds and before the sort. Every body line is the tool's own print of text the same commit added, so the body cannot drift from its diff — the property `Principle-capture:`'s composed one-line-per-change body is built to preserve and the one today's annotation body has by construction — while the marker, the line form and the per-question `lift` call all carry over unchanged from the sweep this pass replaces, so the split costs the commit convention one descriptor and nothing else; because the run writes only the recommendation-less blocks, the body is one line per block this run decided rather than a restatement of the whole document on every re-run, and a block the run judged stale carries its surviving-option verdict into the body for free, the body being exactly those rationales. It restates verbatim what the same commit's diff adds, at the run's full scale — a first pass over a set this size stacks fourteen rationales — and records only the per-block picks, so whatever whole-set reasoning became neither a rationale clause nor a `<depends-on>` element is kept nowhere; and the marker's readability rests on the still-open `Alternatives pass commit subject and body` taking the matching `Alternatives-annotation:` form, since a sibling marker outside that family would leave `Recommendation-annotation:` naming a half whose counterpart is unnamed.

Same subject, but the body is free prose the pass composes once for the run: how it read the set as a whole, which picks turned on which siblings, and what it did with any block it could not settle. It is the only shape that records the thing this pass exists to produce and the diff cannot show — the cross-question reasoning behind a set of picks made together, including the couplings weighed and rejected that never became an element — and it stays one short paragraph whatever the question count, where per-question lines grow with the set. It is composed text backed by no tool print, unique among the plugin's bodies (every other is a tool's own line, a heading, or the user's own words), so nothing pins it to the diff it describes and an over-long or hedged paragraph has no check; and it gives up the per-decision grep line every answer and annotation commit in the log carries today.

Same subject with a two-part body: a short composed paragraph on the whole-set reasoning and any block the run left unsettled, then the lifted line per annotated question beneath it. Each half records what only it can — the tool's lines for what the document now holds, one paragraph for the run-level reasoning and the skips a diff cannot show — and neither half is new to the repo, the lines being today's body and the paragraph the `Principle-capture:` body's composed-at-commit-time form. It is the plugin's first two-part commit body, so the skill must specify both halves and the boundary between them, and the paragraph's content is largely the union of clauses the lines below already carry — the composed half most likely to be written as a summary of the very lines it sits above, which is redundancy carrying the drift risk without either half's strength.

The body of the first option under a new marker naming what the pass now does — for instance `Recommendation-pick: <milestone_id>` — leaving `Recommendation-annotation:` to the pre-split commits that embedded a whole analysis at once. It keeps one marker meaning one payload across the whole history, which matters precisely here because the split changes what such a commit holds — a run's picks against frozen alternatives rather than one question's alternatives and pick together — and the commit convention derives markers from distinctive function with no grandfathered exceptions. It breaks the pairing the split's own vocabulary creates, two annotating passes whose markers differ in exactly the word naming their half, and it buys a distinction the descriptor already makes plain (a Short Title before the split, a milestone id after) at the price of one more prefix a log reader must learn and every doc surface must name.
open-question.recommendation: The pass writes a recommendation per block, so the record git keeps should be per block too, and the lifted line is that record already written and already printed by the tool rather than composed a second time as prose nothing pins to the diff; keeping `Recommendation-annotation:` names the half this pass owns beside its alternatives sibling, and swapping the descriptor to the milestone id is what every once-per-run committer here already does, so the split costs the commit convention one word; only if a run's whole-set reasoning routinely failed to fit inside the rationales that run produced would the lead paragraph be worth its drift risk.

open-question.id: Alternatives pass commit subject and body
open-question.question: /provide-alternatives-to-all-open-questions embeds and commits each return as it lands. What is its commit subject (for example Alternatives-annotation: <Short Title>), what if anything goes in the body given that lift prints only recommendation or single-alternative lines, and what is its one fixed terse success line?
open-question.alternative: Commit each embedded return under `Alternatives-annotation: <Short Title>` with no body at all — the subject-only form `commit-procedure.md` already provides for when a caller supplies no BODY — and report the run with the one fixed line `Alternatives embedded.`, the reporting invariant's own no-op line and still-skipped advisory being the only other output. It answers all three halves from conventions already in the repo and invents nothing: the marker is `Recommendation-annotation:`'s sibling differing in exactly the word that names its half, so the two passes read as the two halves of one annotation and the counterpart the recommendation sibling's drawback leaves unnamed is filled; the descriptor is the Short Title because the commit is per return, exactly as every per-item commit here carries its item's handle while every once-per-run one carries the milestone id; the body is omitted because this half has no one-line tool print to hold — `lift` prints a recommendation or a single named alternative and nothing else — and subject-only commits are ordinary here, `Question-ordering:` among them; and `Alternatives embedded.` is the existing success line with one noun changed, identifier-free as the rule requires. It also stays clear of capture's anchors by construction, since that grep is anchored and its `Alternative-answer` branch cannot match `Alternatives-annotation`. It leaves the one annotation family inconsistent in the log — the recommendation half carries its rationale in the body, this half carries nothing — so `git log` says which questions gained alternatives but never which alternatives, and reviewing a wide parallel run means opening one diff per commit; and the marker sits one letter from `Alternative-answer:`, so a human skim or a loosely written `Alternative-` grep can conflate an annotation with an answer.

Same subject and success line, but give each commit a body of one `lift --alternative "<id>"` line per embedded alternative — "`<id>` — `<what-it-is>`" — the ids recovered after the embed from a `locate` of the block the call just wrote. It holds the whole annotation family's bodies to the single rule the recommendation sibling's pick turns on — every body line is the tool's own print of text the same commit added, so a body cannot drift from its diff — and it puts each question's enumerated option ids in the log where a reviewer scanning a wide parallel run reads them without opening a diff. Nothing the pass already runs prints those ids, so the body costs a `locate` plus a prose read of the printed block to recover them and then one `lift` call per alternative, reintroducing into the busiest loop in the plugin exactly the orchestrator-side reading of a block's contents that this design has otherwise moved into the tool — and what it yields is an unbounded multi-line restatement of the very children the same commit's one-element-per-line canonical diff already shows.

Keep the subject and the success line and give the tool a whole-block alternatives print — for example `lift --alternatives "<Short Title>"`, one "`<id>` — `<what-it-is>`" line per alternative — so this half's body is one tool call, as the recommendation half's is. It recovers a tool-printed, drift-proof body in exactly one call per commit with no reading of the block by the pass at all, and the same print would serve any later consumer needing a block's option roster without a `locate`. It widens the tool — a new flag, its refusal strings and its own test coverage — beyond the three tool changes the goal names, and does so for a commit body alone, producing text that is a second copy of the diff it rides in, which is the thinnest reason in this repo to add a tool surface.

Derive the marker from the pass's own name rather than from the sweep it splits off — `Alternatives-provision: <Short Title>`, or `Alternatives-enumeration:` — with the body and the success line as in the first option. It derives the marker straight from the skill's distinctive function the way the commit convention asks of a new marker, and it puts a whole word between this marker and `Alternative-answer:`, so no log skim or hand-written grep can conflate the two. It breaks the pairing the split's own vocabulary creates — two annotating passes whose markers differ in exactly the word naming their half — leaving `Recommendation-annotation:` reading as a leftover rather than one of a pair, and it buys separation from an answer marker no automated reader can confuse, since capture's grep is both-ends-anchored and names its three branches literally.

depends-on.question: Recommendation run commit subject and body

open-question.recommendation: The split produces two annotating halves, so their markers should differ in exactly the word that names the half — `Alternatives-annotation: <Short Title>` per return beside `Recommendation-annotation: <milestone_id>` per run, the descriptor following the commit's granularity as it already does everywhere here — and the body is left empty because this half has no one-line tool print to put in it and every substitute is either a block read the tool was built to absorb or a restatement of the same commit's diff, while `Alternatives embedded.` is the existing success line with one noun changed; only if a reviewer routinely had to know a block's option ids from the log alone, without opening the diff, would adding the whole-block print be worth its tool surface.
